title: QUIC Non-HTTP/3 Interop-Testcase Inventory Architecture
purpose: Describe the canonical inventory/profile that records every documented non-HTTP/3 interop testcase as an explicit harness cell classification instead of collapsing the remaining cases into a generic unsupported fallthrough.
design_summary: The documented upstream QUIC testcase set is treated as a canonical inventory/profile, with each testcase assigned to one of four explicit classes: supported and executed, intentionally represented as unsupported with exit code 127, blocked by a named prerequisite, or not mappable through the current helper/workflow shape. The current helper-supported cells are handshake, transfer, longrtt, multiplexing, retry, multiconnect, versionnegotiation, chacha20, keyupdate, resumption, zerortt, amplificationlimit, blackhole, transferloss, ipv6, and connectionmigration. The transfer-derived cells reuse the existing HTTP/0.9 transfer, recovery, and endpoint-host paths until live proof says otherwise, while v2, rebind-port, and rebind-addr remain prerequisite-blocked. Resumption is green only for the runner TLS session-resumption cell with managed SSLKEYLOGFILE export proof; HTTP/3, corruption-test, ECN, anti-replay, and broader public API support remain out of scope. The chacha20 cell now has runnable helper dispatch branches and preserved local runner proof, while zerortt has preserved hosted/Linux proof; both cells stay bounded to the checked runner evidence and do not imply HTTP/3 or broader API support. The server-role harness path enables managed resumption tickets plus server early-data admission for runner-driven attempts, and the manual hosted workflow exposes an advisory `zerortt-server-proof` profile so Linux runner evidence can be captured beyond the 2026-05-09 local Windows long-filename setup blocker. Hosted run `25608915721` reached managed server execution and quic-go second-connection 0-RTT emission, but it also proved the former first-flight key-share/HelloRetryRequest incompatibility: the then-current P-256-only crypto floor sent HRR for quic-go's hybrid/X25519 offer, and quic-go treated that HRR as 0-RTT rejection. REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154 now locally proves bounded server first-flight X25519 acceptance for that captured offer. Hosted run `25617591021` confirmed the key-share/HRR blocker had moved forward but exposed a queued-final STREAM+FIN flush failure under transient congestion; commit `e7dece89` fixed that runtime path with focused RFC 9000 stream-send coverage. Hosted run `25617834482` then reached managed response/download success, but runner post-analysis still failed with `0-RTT size: 10618`, `1-RTT size: 16499`, and `Client sent too much data in 1-RTT packets.` The inventory/profile exists so the repository can work the remaining non-HTTP/3 cases down case-by-case without overclaiming support readiness or silently hiding them behind a generic unsupported fallback.
alternatives_considered: Keep the remaining non-HTTP/3 cases hidden behind a generic unsupported exit. Rejected because the request is to make the full suite visible as an explicit goal, not to bury it.
Treat the inventory/profile as a new protocol-support promise. Rejected because the slice is about explicit classification and evidence retention, not about turning every testcase green immediately.
edge_cases_and_constraints: HTTP/3 stays out of scope for this inventory/profile.
The inventory must distinguish supported cells from intentionally unsupported, prerequisite-blocked, and currently non-mappable cells.
A cell classified as unsupported must do so explicitly and honestly; it must not be implied by omission.
The inventory must not be read as a broad interop-readiness claim.
data_and_state_considerations: The inventory/profile is primarily static trace data plus per-cell dry-run or execution artifacts. It should remain separable from protocol runtime state and from the current supported-subset artifact bundles.
risks: The documented upstream testcase surface may drift if quic-interop-runner changes its QUIC docs.
Readers may mistake explicit inventory coverage for green support unless the classification labels stay prominent.
Some cases are blocked by runtime prerequisites outside the harness, so the profile must not collapse them into a generic unsupported bucket.

supplemental_sections.heading: Inventory Model
supplemental_sections.content: Current documented non-HTTP/3 cases include versionnegotiation, handshake, transfer, longrtt, chacha20, multiplexing, keyupdate, retry, resumption, zerortt, amplificationlimit, blackhole, multiconnect, transferloss, ipv6, v2, rebind-port, rebind-addr, and connectionmigration. The inventory/profile records the current class for each case, with versionnegotiation, handshake, transfer, longrtt, chacha20, multiplexing, keyupdate, retry, resumption, zerortt, amplificationlimit, blackhole, multiconnect, transferloss, ipv6, and connectionmigration now supported/executed while v2, rebind-port, and rebind-addr remain prerequisite-blocked. Corruption-test and ECN cells stay outside this helper-supported inventory until separate proof promotes them. Hosted run `25617834482` reached managed response/download success after the prior X25519 and queued-final-stream fixes, but the runner still failed packet analysis because too much data used 1-RTT packets. The chacha20 lane is now closed by the local quic-go/quic-go runner proof under `artifacts/interop-runner/20260513-011027614-both-quic-go/runner-report.json`, and the internal admission-gate proof under ARC-QUIC-CRT-0048, bounded internal early-data runtime proof under ARC-QUIC-CRT-0049, local X25519 proof under ARC-QUIC-CRT-0050, runtime queued-final-stream proof under the RFC 9000 stream-send home, and server-role runner dispatch are necessary but not support evidence by themselves. Resumption is limited to the checked runner TLS session-resumption cell with SSLKEYLOGFILE-backed proof. Cases can move from blocked or unsupported to executed as the underlying protocol slices land.
